No confidence band is shown.

speechChecks.text:
×
Moses & Chang

Speech decoding

2021 · reference-year placement; source date below

Text-equivalent / native-task context (bits/s · log): ≈1.27

Reported input: Neuroprosthesis for Decoding Speech in a Paralyzed Person with Anarthria ↗

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 15.2 words/minute; real-time visually prompted sentence decoding, language model enabled. 25.6% word error rate. 15.2 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × 1 assumed bit/character ÷ 60. PL R&D estimate of gross decoding pace under a context-dependent English-entropy model; five characters/word includes spaces. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 1.2 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2021-07-14 (first online publication; issue 2021-07-15). Prompted sentences with a language model and a restricted 50-word vocabulary. WPM and WER are source-level medians with different aggregation, not a per-trial channel estimate. Text-equivalent; fit included.

Calculation source: Stanford · Entropy and Redundancy in English ↗

×
Willett et al. · speech

Speech decoding

2023 · reference-year placement; source date below

Text-equivalent / native-task context (bits/s · log): ≈5.17

Reported input: A high-performance speech neuroprosthesis ↗

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 62 words/minute; real-time held-out prompted sentences. 23.8% word error rate. 62 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × 1 assumed bit/character ÷ 60. PL R&D estimate of gross decoding pace under a context-dependent English-entropy model; five characters/word includes spaces. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 4.9 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2023-08-23 (first online publication). The 23.8% WER applies to the 125,000-word vocalized condition; the paper's 9.1% WER belongs to a separate 50-word condition. Evaluation used held-out prompted sentences, not free conversation. Text-equivalent; fit included.

Calculation source: Stanford · Entropy and Redundancy in English ↗

×
Metzger & Chang

Speech decoding

2023 · reference-year placement; source date below

Text-equivalent / native-task context (bits/s · log): ≈6.53

Reported input: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control ↗

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 78.3 words/minute; real-time text decoding of held-out silently attempted prompted sentences. 25.5% word error rate. 78.3 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × 1 assumed bit/character ÷ 60. PL R&D estimate of gross decoding pace under a context-dependent English-entropy model; five characters/word includes spaces. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 6.2 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2023-08-23 (first online publication). Online evaluation used 1,024 words. The 39,378-word condition was an offline simulation; a later anatomical correction did not change real-time decoding performance. Text-equivalent; fit included.

Calculation source: Stanford · Entropy and Redundancy in English ↗

×
Card & Stavisky

Speech decoding

2024 · reference-year placement; source date below

Text-equivalent / native-task context (bits/s · log): ≈2.63

Reported input: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis ↗

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 31.6 words/minute; prompted copy task at self-paced speaking rate. 2.5% word error rate. 31.6 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × 1 assumed bit/character ÷ 60. PL R&D estimate of gross decoding pace under a context-dependent English-entropy model; five characters/word includes spaces. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 2.6 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2024-08-14 (first online publication; issue 2024-08-15). 31.6 WPM and 2.5% WER are the final five copy-task session means. The reference figure's 33-WPM label is a different, unverified selection. Text-equivalent; fit included.

Calculation source: Stanford · Entropy and Redundancy in English ↗

×
Card & Stavisky · home use

Speech decoding

2025 · reference-year placement; source date below

Text-equivalent / native-task context (bits/s · log): ≈4.67

Reported input: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control ↗

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 56.1 words/minute; unconstrained personal use at home. 56.1 words/minute × 5 assumed characters/word × 1 assumed bit/character ÷ 60. PL R&D estimate of gross decoding pace under a context-dependent English-entropy model; five characters/word includes spaces. No error penalty; the reported error metric remains separate. Reference image: approximately 4.4 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2025-07-07 (bioRxiv v1 posting, not DOI date string; peer-reviewed online publication 2026-06-15). Personal home use has no paired WER here. The 99.2% copy-task accuracy and 92.3% participant-rated sentence correctness are different endpoints. This follows the same participant as Card 2024, not an independent cohort. Text-equivalent; fit included.

Calculation source: Stanford · Entropy and Redundancy in English ↗

state.handwritingUnchanged:
×
Willett et al. · handwriting

Handwriting decoding

2021 · reference-year placement; source date below

Text-equivalent / native-task context (bits/s · log): ≈7.21

Reported input: High-performance brain-to-text communication via handwriting ↗

PL R&D estimate. Reported input: 90 characters/minute with 5.4% character error rate on the final evaluation day, from Willett et al. 2021. 90 characters/minute × log2(28) bits/character ÷ 60. PL R&D code-equivalent estimate of gross decoding pace, not measured neural ITR. No error penalty; 5.4% CER remains separate. Reference image: approximately 6.6 bits/s; original image coordinates remain archived separately. Publication/disclosure: 2021-05-12 (first online publication; issue 2021-05-13). The final-day 5.4% character error rate is distinct from the overall five-day 94.1% accuracy. The selected 90-CPM gross pace is converted by PL R&D without a CER penalty; no author corrected-typing model is used. Text-equivalent; fit included.
